extracted.intended_audience: comic-book publishers, historians, researchers of censorship and the general public interested in comics history
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and summarize the content-regulation standards published by the Association of Comics Magazine Publishers (ACMP) — the 1948 Publishers Code — and related practices around approval/seals and enforcement. Focus is on historical content rules for comic-book publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexy, wanton comics should not be published
rubrics_metrics.description: Sexy, wanton comics should not be published. No drawing should show a female indecently or unduly exposed, and in no event more nude than in a bathing suit commonly worn in the United States of America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule prohibits overt sexualization and explicit nudity; the page ties it to the broader phrase 'sexy, wanton comics' used in the 1948 ACMP Publishers Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime portrayal must not throw sympathy against the law or inspire imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Crime should not be presented in such a way as to throw sympathy against the law and justice or to inspire others with the desire for imitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeled on the Hays Production Code approach: stories must not glamorize criminal behavior or encourage readers to emulate crime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not show details or methods of crimes committed by youths
rubrics_metrics.description: No comics shall show the details and methods of a crime committed by a youth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit prohibition on instructional depictions of how crimes are committed when the perpetrator is a youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for authority in portrayals of officials and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Policemen, judges, Government officials, and respected institutions should not be portrayed as stupid, ineffective, or represented in such a way to weaken respect for established authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits ridicule or undermining of legal/governmental authority and respected institutions; intended to maintain social deference to authority figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: No scenes of sadistic torture
rubrics_metrics.description: No scenes of sadistic torture should be shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute ban on graphic sadism/torture imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban on vulgar and obscene language; limit slang
rubrics_metrics.description: Vulgar and obscene language should never be used. Slang should be kept to a minimum and used only when essential to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language standards prohibit obscenity entirely and restrict colloquial/slang usage to necessary narrative contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divorce must not be trivialized or glamorized
rubrics_metrics.description: Divorce should not be treated humorously or represented as glamorous or alluring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides depiction of sensitive social topics to avoid glamorization or flippant treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No ridicule or attack on religious or racial groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Ridicule or attack on any religious or racial group is never permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit non-discrimination clause forbidding derogatory portrayals of protected groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seal of Approval offered for compliant comics
rubrics_metrics.description: Comics that complied with the code were offered a 'Seal of Approval.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural/quality indicator: the Seal signaled compliance. The article notes enforcement was weak—many publishers ignored the code, some used the seal without formal review, and the association and code were effectively out of business by 1954.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition (as recalled) on certain genre words (e.g., 'horror','terror','weird')
rubrics_metrics.description: According to William M. Gaines (1983 interview), the Code forbade the use of the words 'horror,' 'terror,' 'crime' and even 'weird' (this recollection pertains to the era's code enforcement and its effects on publishers like EC Comics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anecdotal/example-based prohibition reported by a publisher: banning particular words functioned as a content-control mechanism and—per Gaines—had strong commercial consequences through distribution/wholesaler actions. This item is drawn from a publisher's retrospective quote rather than the bullet-code text.
